title: Write interlocking guards only in the declarative guard grammar

facts.note: Subject kind is 'interlocking'; an observer must find train/interlocking definitions that contain guard expressions. The source names no path glob.
The validator runs at CONFIRM and blocks confirmation. It checks every interlocking guard, including unchanged ones.
This is an extra trigger, not a required condition. A diff-level observer can flag guard edits early while the plan is being written. Unchanged guards are still in scope at CONFIRM.

fires: A planner adds or edits a guard expression on a train interlocking.
CONFIRM validation runs over a plan whose interlockings contain guards, including guards that were not changed.
A guard uses arbitrary executable Python (eval, a function call other than exists(field), a lambda, a method call) or an operator outside the allowed set.
A guard reads a TrainResult that is not completed or is not at a declared route boundary.
The CONFIRM grammar validator reports an invalid token in an interlocking guard.
doesNotFire: Plans or trains that declare no interlocking guard expressions.
Plan prose or acceptance text that is not an interlocking guard expression.

given: A train interlocking declares guard expressions
when: the planner writes or edits a guard, or the plan reaches CONFIRM
then: Every guard uses only the guard grammar. Inputs: action/request inputs, an explicit state snapshot, and a completed TrainResult only at declared route boundaries. Operators: == != < <= > >= and or not exists(field) in.
prefer: Pure comparisons and boolean combinations over declared input and snapshot fields.
exists(field) to test whether a field is present.
Pass needed data through the explicit state snapshot.
avoid: Raw Python eval or arbitrary executable code: calls other than exists(field), imports, lambdas, method calls, comprehensions. Plain references to allowed input fields are fine.
Side effects or non-deterministic inputs (time, randomness, environment, I/O).
Reading a TrainResult that is not completed or is outside a declared route boundary.
Disguising disallowed tokens to get past the validator.
why: Guards decide routing. Declarative, deterministic, side-effect-free guards keep routes reproducible and statically checkable. Raw eval allows arbitrary code execution.
evidence: The CONFIRM validator (test_sequence_diagram_sanity::test_interlocking_guard_grammar_is_safe) passes for every interlocking guard.
Every guard token is an allowed input reference, a literal, or one of: == != < <= > >= and or not exists(field) in.
On failure, the report names interlocking_id, guard_id, expression, invalid_token and reason.
verifier_detail: Validation family: grammar; template: identifier_grammar_conformance; variant: planner_train_interlocking_guard_grammar; subject_kind: interlocking.
Phase: CONFIRM. Enforcement: confirm-blocking. Severity: 3. Disposition: strict. Scope: all interlocking guards, changed or not.

Allowed operators: == != < <= > >= and or not in, plus the call form exists(field). Field references to allowed inputs are valid. Any other call, operator, or executable construct is an invalid_token.
Allowed inputs: action/request inputs, explicit state snapshot, and a completed TrainResult only at declared route boundaries.
failure_evidence fields: interlocking_id, guard_id, expression, invalid_token, reason.
audit: Term id: guard_grammar (defines the allowed inputs and operators).
Graph: requires planner.train.interlocking-home (the guard grammar is declared on a homed interlocking).

sharedNodes.text: Strict disposition: the convention fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode.

additions.text: Concrete preferred moves (pure comparisons, exists(field) for presence, explicit snapshot).
additions.justification: Turns the allowed grammar into actionable planner moves; adds no new obligation.

additions.justification: Makes 'declarative, deterministic, side-effect-free; raw Python eval forbidden' concrete and covers metric gaming. exists(field) and plain field references remain permitted.
